title: Some Trees Make City Air Quality Worse — Study
paragraphs: When you think of ways to reduce air pollution, one of the first things that probably comes to mind is planting more trees.
But a new study suggests that some tree species can actually worsen air pollution, especially during very hot weather.
Researchers studying air quality in Beijing, China, looked at volatile organic compounds, or VOCs — gases released from vehicles and industrial processes, but also naturally from trees and plants.
Some tree species, like willows and poplars, release especially large amounts of isoprene, a type of VOC. About 35% of Beijing's trees are such species.
VOCs are not necessarily harmful on their own. But in the presence of sunlight they react with nitrogen oxides — pollutants produced by traffic and industry — and help create ground-level ozone.
Unlike the protective ozone layer high above Earth, ground-level ozone — the main ingredient in smog — can damage the lungs and worsen breathing problems.
The researchers had wanted to see how human activities affected ground-level ozone pollution, but the results showing the impact of trees surprised them.
"When we got this data, we did not believe it in the beginning," said study co-author Bin Yuan.
The team found that while vegetation doesn't produce the majority of the VOCs in Beijing, it is disproportionately responsible for ground-level ozone formation.

In air samples taken between May and July 2021, the researchers found that plants produced only about 10% of Beijing's total VOC emissions, while human activities produced the rest. However, plants accounted for 52% of the chemicals that help to form ground-level ozone.

And while heat amplifies the reactivity of all VOCs, this is particularly true for VOCs from plants. At 35 degrees Celsius, the reaction rate of VOCs from trees was 700% higher than at 20 degrees. By comparison, VOC reactivity from human sources was only 40% higher.

Yuan emphasized that the findings do not argue against planting trees. But as climate change brings higher temperatures and more heatwaves, cities may need to think more carefully about which trees they plant.
